### PQB_MSQ_E1: Identify all primary tissue classes in human histology: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Epithelial Tissue
- [ ] B) Connective Tissue
- [ ] C) Muscular Tissue
- [ ] D) Nervous Tissue
- [ ] E) Bone tissue only

> **✅ Answers:** A) Epithelial Tissue, B) Connective Tissue, C) Muscular Tissue, D) Nervous Tissue
> **Explanation:** 4 primary tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, Nervous.

### PQB_MSQ_E2: Which cell junctions join adjacent epithelial cells together? (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Tight junction
- [ ] B) Adherens junction
- [ ] C) Desmosome
- [ ] D) Gap junction
- [ ] E) Synaptic terminal

> **✅ Answers:** A) Tight junction, B) Adherens junction, C) Desmosome, D) Gap junction
> **Explanation:** Epithelial junctions = Tight, Adherens, Desmosome, Gap.

### PQB_MSQ_E3: Identify all formed blood elements in circulating bloodstream: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Erythrocytes (RBC)
- [ ] B) Leucocytes (WBC)
- [ ] C) Thrombocytes (Platelets)
- [ ] D) Albumins
- [ ] E) Fibrinogen

> **✅ Answers:** A) Erythrocytes (RBC), B) Leucocytes (WBC), C) Thrombocytes (Platelets)
> **Explanation:** Formed elements = RBC, WBC, Platelets.

### PQB_MSQ_E4: Identify all features belonging to Skeletal Muscle histology: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Voluntary control
- [ ] B) Multinucleated syncytium
- [ ] C) Striated bands
- [ ] D) Intercalated discs
- [ ] E) Rapid fatigue

> **✅ Answers:** A) Voluntary control, B) Multinucleated syncytium, C) Striated bands, E) Rapid fatigue
> **Explanation:** Skeletal muscle is voluntary, syncytial, striated, subject to fatigue.

### PQB_MSQ_E5: Which structures contain Hyaline Cartilage extracellular matrix? (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Articular ends of long bones
- [ ] B) Nasal septum
- [ ] C) Costal cartilage of ribs
- [ ] D) Intervertebral discs
- [ ] E) Tracheal rings

> **✅ Answers:** A) Articular ends of long bones, B) Nasal septum, C) Costal cartilage of ribs, E) Tracheal rings
> **Explanation:** Hyaline cartilage lines articular ends, nose, ribs, trachea.

- [ ] C) Lining of gall bladder
- [ ] D) Lining of Fallopian tubes (Ciliated variant)

### PQB_MSQ_E7: In Question Bank Easy deck, select all key properties of Connective Tissue: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Abundant extracellular matrix
- [ ] B) Vascular blood supply in CT proper
- [ ] C) Connects and supports other tissues
- [ ] D) Derived from embryonic mesoderm
- [ ] E) Avascular tightly packed sheets with no matrix

> **✅ Answers:** A) Abundant extracellular matrix, B) Vascular blood supply in CT proper, C) Connects and supports other tissues, D) Derived from embryonic mesoderm
> **Explanation:** Connective tissue has abundant matrix, vascular supply (except cartilage), mesodermal origin.

### PQB_MSQ_E8: In Question Bank Easy deck, identify all functions of Leucocytes (WBCs): (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Bacterial phagocytosis by Neutrophils
- [ ] B) Antibody production by Lymphocytes
- [ ] C) Histamine release by Basophils
- [ ] D) Parasitic defense by Eosinophils
- [ ] E) Oxygen transport by Hemoglobin

> **✅ Answers:** A) Bacterial phagocytosis by Neutrophils, B) Antibody production by Lymphocytes, C) Histamine release by Basophils, D) Parasitic defense by Eosinophils
> **Explanation:** WBCs perform immune protection via phagocytosis, antibody production, and inflammatory defense.

### PQB_MSQ_E9: In Question Bank Easy deck, select all structural parts of a typical Multipolar Neurone: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Cell body Cyton / Soma
- [ ] B) Receptive Dendrites
- [ ] C) Single conducting Axon
- [ ] D) Protein-synthesizing Nissl's granules
- [ ] E) Contractile Sarcomeres

> **✅ Answers:** A) Cell body Cyton / Soma, B) Receptive Dendrites, C) Single conducting Axon, D) Protein-synthesizing Nissl's granules
> **Explanation:** Neurones consist of Cyton, Dendrites, Axon, and Nissl's granules.

### PQB_MSQ_E10: In Question Bank Easy deck, select all exocrine glands classified by morphology: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Unicellular Goblet glands
- [ ] B) Simple tubular sweat glands
- [ ] C) Compound alveolar salivary glands
- [ ] D) Compound tubulo-alveolar pancreas glands
- [ ] E) Ductless pituitary thyroid glands

> **✅ Answers:** A) Unicellular Goblet glands, B) Simple tubular sweat glands, C) Compound alveolar salivary glands, D) Compound tubulo-alveolar pancreas glands
> **Explanation:** Exocrine glands include unicellular goblet cells, simple tubular, compound alveolar, and tubulo-alveolar glands.
